tasks.title: Parallel-execution RFC
tasks.description: Write a design RFC (new doc: `docs/parallel-execution-rfc.md`) for running multiple dependency-free tasks concurrently. Must cover: (1) ISOLATION MODEL — git worktrees-per-task vs directory-disjoint scheduling, with trade-offs, left as the central OPEN decision rather than pre-committed; (2) SCHEDULING — a plural ready-set selector capped at N with conflict filtering; (3) OUTPUT RENDERING for N concurrent agents (task-id line prefixes / per-task logs / sectioned view); (4) NARRATION & NOTIFICATIONS — in parallel mode drop per-agent streaming narration, narrate lifecycle milestones only (started/completed/failed) via a queue, batch ntfy into wave summaries; serial mode keeps full streaming; (5) KNOCK-ON EFFECTS — `prevNotes` carry-forward (no single predecessor per wave), the per-iteration `tasks.json` snapshot (`src/commands/run.ts` ~line 454), test-validation timing, and post-task review under parallelism; (6) ROLLOUT — opt-in flag (e.g. `--parallel N`) with serial as default. Ground it in current serial behavior: `selectNextTask` (`src/task-selector.ts`), focused commits in the shared working tree (`src/commands/run.ts` ~line 548), unlocked `mutateTasksFile` (`src/tasks-file.ts`), single-socket narration (`src/narration.ts`). Documentation only — no code or tests.
tasks.notes:
# Task #6 Completion Notes: Parallel-execution RFC

## What was done

Created `docs/parallel-execution-rfc.md` (350 lines). Documentation only — no
code or tests, as the task specified.

## Structure

The RFC is grounded throughout in the *current serial behavior*, with concrete
file:line references so the design is anchored to real code:

- §2 baseline catalogs every serial assumption: single `selectNextTask`
  (`src/task-selector.ts:44`), single `spawnClaude` shared-tree agent
  (`src/commands/run.ts:184`), focused commits in the shared tree
  (`src/commands/run.ts:129`), unlocked `mutateTasksFile`
  (`src/tasks-file.ts:174`), per-iteration snapshot
  (`src/commands/run.ts:454`), single narration socket (`src/narration.ts`),
  single `prevNotes` predecessor (`src/commands/run.ts:624`).

All six required topics are covered:

1. **§3 Isolation model** — Option A (git worktree per task) vs Option B
   (directory-disjoint shared tree), full pros/cons, left as THE central OPEN
   decision with a decision *procedure* rather than a verdict. Rest of doc
   written isolation-agnostic, flagging where it depends on the choice.
2. **§4 Scheduling** — plural `selectReadyTasks` selector capped at N, reusing
   today's readiness rule, with conflict filtering (dependency-internal +
   footprint). Also covers wave-vs-rolling; recommends wave first.
3. **§5 Output rendering** — task-id line prefixes (baseline) + per-task log
   files + optional sectioned TUI gated on isTTY.
4. **§6 Narration & notifications** — parallel mode drops per-agent streaming
   narration, narrates lifecycle milestones (started/completed/failed) via a
   serialized queue, batches ntfy into wave summaries; serial mode unchanged.
5. **§7 Knock-on effects** — prevNotes carry-forward (no single predecessor),
   per-iteration snapshot timing, the cross-process `mutateTasksFile` race
   (flagged as the sharpest hazard + lock prerequisite), test-validation
   timing, post-task review diff attribution under both isolation options.
6. **§8 Rollout** — opt-in `--parallel N`, serial as default and preserved
   verbatim, independently-shippable work sequence, `--parallel 1` kill switch.

§9 summarizes the open questions, with the isolation model as #1.

## Notable design stances taken (for reviewer awareness)

- Recommends adding a cross-process lock to `mutateTasksFile` as a standalone
  prerequisite — safe for serial mode too, so it can land first.
- Recommends wave (barrier) execution before rolling concurrency.
- Recommends `--parallel 1` be behaviorally identical to serial as the core
  compatibility guarantee.

## Tests

None — documentation only.

tasks.title: Concurrency-safe tasks.json writes
tasks.description: Make `src/tasks-file.ts` writes safe under concurrent writers (each Ralph agent shells `ralph task ...`, so this MUST be cross-process safe). Two fixes: (a) give each write a per-process UNIQUE tmp path instead of the shared `${filePath}.tmp` (used in both `writeTasksFile` ~line 164 and the `finally` cleanup in `mutateTasksFile` ~line 180) — e.g. incorporate `process.pid` plus a crypto/random suffix so concurrent writers never clobber the same tmp file; (b) add a cross-process FILE LOCK around the read->modify->write critical section in `mutateTasksFile` — acquire via an `O_EXCL` lockfile (e.g. `${filePath}.lock`) with bounded retry/backoff, release it in a `finally`, and surface a clear error if the lock can't be acquired. Keep the existing snapshot-after-write behavior. TDD: add a failing concurrent-writer test to `test/tasks-file.test.ts` FIRST (interleave multiple `mutateTasksFile` calls mutating distinct fields and assert no lost updates and no JSON corruption), watch it fail, then implement.

tasks.title: Plural ready-set selector
tasks.description: Add `selectReadyTasks(tasks: Task[], completedIds: Set<number>, opts?: { limit?: number }): Task[]` to `src/task-selector.ts` alongside the existing `selectNextTask` (which stays unchanged for serial mode). It returns a batch of pending tasks whose dependencies are ALL satisfied (use the same active+archived complete-id logic as `selectNextTask`, ~lines 51-54), sorted by priority ascending, capped at `opts.limit`, and conflict-filtered so the returned set has no two tasks sharing the same non-empty `directory` (a wave must never have two agents writing the same dir). Decide AND document in a code comment how in-progress tasks interact with the ready-set (e.g. lead with them, or treat their directories as occupied). TDD: add failing tests to `test/task-selector.test.ts` FIRST covering dependency gating, priority ordering, limit capping, and directory-conflict exclusion; watch them fail, then implement.

tasks.title: Task-id-labeled stream output
tasks.description: Thread an optional task id through the stream filter in `src/stream-filter.ts` so concurrent agents' lines can be prefixed `[#id]`. Add an optional field (e.g. `taskId?: number` or `linePrefix?: string`) to `ProcessStreamOptions` (~line 163) and, when set, prefix each emitted output line with `[#<id>] `. When unset, output must be byte-for-byte unchanged (serial mode MUST NOT regress). TDD: add failing tests to `test/stream-filter.test.ts` FIRST — one asserting lines are prefixed when the id is provided, one asserting identical output to today when it is omitted; watch them fail, then implement.
